description: Team focusing on Earth Science and AI applications using NASA open data. Our background covers satellite data analytics and machine learning. We welcome collaborators skilled in front-end development, data visualization, or product design to join forces for Hanoi Hackathon 2026!
summary:
We built an interactive web map and documentation site for Hung Yen province, Vietnam (merged with Thai Binh in 2025; about 2,570 km² of rice fields, aquaculture ponds, dikes and villages). It uses three NISAR L-band GCOV VALIDATED acquisitions (Oct 22, Oct 27, Nov 3, 2026) to answer two questions: what changed, and what is on the ground, using SAR alone.
For change detection we ran a speckle-aware statistical test on the two same-track dates: 99.89% of the area is unchanged, and one significant patch stands out, about 1.6 km² of new open water near 106.484°E, 20.463°N (HH dropped from -10 to -16 dB). Its cause is a hypothesis (flooded pond, field or dike enclosure), not verified, because clouds blocked optical confirmation.
For land cover we trained a SAR-only 4-class classifier (water, vegetation, bare land, built-up) and compared 14 models in 8 experiments. Balanced accuracy is about 93% on pure cells under 5-km spatial block cross-validation. We also publish an applicability layer and model agreement so users see where the map is unreliable. Everything is open and bilingual (EN/VI).
details:
WHAT IT DOES

A full-screen web map (https://dwts.ninhhaidang.com) with: a 3-date SAR viewer with swipe/slider comparison, a statistically tested change layer, a 4-class SAR-only land cover layer with a model-agreement layer and an "outside applicability area" overlay, labeled polygons, click-to-query pixel time series (HH/HV in dB for all three dates), ~25 pages of bilingual docs, and a documentation-grounded chatbot.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Data: NISAR L2 GCOV frequency A (HHHH, HVHV), cropped to the area of interest. Oct 22 and Nov 3 are the same descending track 148 at 20 m; Oct 27 is ascending track 054 at 10 m. Oct 29 was dropped (covers 4% of the AOI).

2. Change detection: log-ratio test between the two same-geometry dates, z > 5, minimum patch 0.05 km², with a correction for speckle correlation (effective factor about 1.6-1.7). Result: one significant patch (about 1.6 km² new water), HH -10 to -16 dB and HV -17 to -23 dB, already dropping on Oct 27.

3. Land cover: 1,347 hand-drawn polygons (190 water, 485 vegetation, 444 bare land, 228 built-up), drawn over Sentinel-2 imagery. Only SAR features go into the model (12 features from 3 dates, HH+HV). Random Forest, 3,918 pure 20 m training cells.

4. Experiments: 14 models (top 11 within 0.6 points, 93.0-93.6%), 1 vs 3 dates (83-86% vs 93%), feature ablation, learning curve, nested tuning, and validation design. Random cell splits inflate accuracy by about 3 points; a north/south split drops it to 84-87%.

HONEST LIMITS (we report these on the site)

- 93% is measured on pure cells with spatial block CV, NOT map accuracy. There is no independent test set.

- 8.3% of the area is outside the applicability area, and the built-up class is the least reliable (23.5% of built-up predictions fall outside it).

- The cause of the new water patch is unverified. No clear rice-harvest signal was found in the 12-day window.

TOOLS

Python (rasterio, h5py, scikit-learn, CatBoost, scipy, seaborn), QGIS/ArcGIS Pro for labeling, Google Earth Engine (Sentinel-2 composite), Astro + Starlight, React, MapLibre GL, geotiff.js, Docker, Caddy, Cloudflare Tunnel. Source code (Apache 2.0): https://github.com/ninhhaidang/ns05005-dancing-with-the-sars

CREATIVITY

Instead of one number, we ship the uncertainty: model agreement, applicability area, and the experiments showing which validation choices inflate accuracy. The chatbot answers from the project's own docs and queries pixel values by function calling.

SI DISCLOSURE

Anthropic's Claude (Claude Code) was used for code, debugging, analysis scripts, web app development, documentation drafting and EN/VI translation. The chatbot in the web app uses a Gemini model via an API. All analysis decisions, labeling, and results were reviewed by the team. Code files and docs generated with SI are acknowledged in the repository README. Claude also drafted the presentation slides (layout, text, and two map figures plotted by code from our data); the team then edited them by hand.
